steps.title: Import Angular modules and dependencies
steps.instruction: Import Component, Injectable, and OnInit from '@angular/core'
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple Angular core features
import { Component, Injectable, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode: // Import the required Angular modules and dependencies
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core features needed for creating services and components are imported.
successCriteria: Component, Injectable, and OnInit are imported from '@angular/core'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the essential Angular core modules needed for this RBAC permission hook lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing all three symbols: Component, Injectable, and OnInit from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are not quite right. Remember to import Component, Injectable, and OnInit from the '@angular/core' module.

steps.title: Create a PermissionService with role-based logic
steps.instruction: Create an Angular service called PermissionService with a method named hasPermission that takes a user role and a required permission, and returns a boolean indicating if the user has that permission.
steps.hint: Use the @Injectable decorator to make the service injectable. The hasPermission method should compare the user's role against the required permission.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the required Angular modules and dependencies

// Create the PermissionService here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a PermissionService class with a hasPermission method that implements basic RBAC logic.
successCriteria: PermissionService is created with @Injectable decorator and has a hasPermission method that accepts role and permission parameters and returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the PermissionService with the hasPermission method. This service will handle our RBAC permission checks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your service has the @Injectable decorator and the hasPermission method with proper parameters and return type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service doesn't match the requirements. Remember to create a PermissionService class with @Injectable decorator and a hasPermission method that takes role and permission parameters.

steps.title: Define user roles and permissions interface
steps.instruction: Below the PermissionService class, create a TypeScript interface named 'UserRole' with a 'name' property of type string and a 'permissions' property that is an array of strings.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: A UserRole interface is created with proper TypeScript type definitions for role-based access control.
successCriteria: The UserRole interface exists with 'name: string' and 'permissions: string[]' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the UserRole interface with proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the interface, but make sure it has both 'name' (string) and 'permissions' (string array) properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserRole interface is not properly defined. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword and include both required properties with correct types.

steps.title: Implement permission check method in service
steps.instruction: Add a hasPermission method to your PermissionService that takes a permission string and returns a boolean.
steps.hint: Define a method that accepts a permission parameter and returns true or false based on role logic.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PermissionService will have a hasPermission method that can check permissions.
successCriteria: PermissionService contains a hasPermission method that accepts a string and returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the permission check method to the service.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it accepts a permission string and returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hasPermission method is missing or doesn't match the required signature.

steps.title: Create a PermissionDirective for template-level checks
steps.instruction: Create an Angular directive named PermissionDirective that will be used to conditionally show or hide elements in templates based on user permissions.
steps.hint: Use the @Directive decorator to define a directive. You'll need to inject the PermissionService and implement the logic later.
steps.expectedOutcome: A PermissionDirective class is created with the @Directive decorator, ready to be implemented with permission logic.
successCriteria: The PermissionDirective class is defined with the @Directive decorator and has a basic structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the PermissionDirective. This directive will allow you to control element visibility in templates based on user permissions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the directive, but make sure it has the @Directive decorator and is properly exported as a class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The directive wasn't created correctly. Remember to use the @Directive decorator and export a class named PermissionDirective.

steps.title: Set up the main component structure
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component class named 'PermissionDemoComponent' with the basic structure including the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define the component metadata, including a selector and an empty template string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new component class named PermissionDemoComponent is created with the @Component decorator and basic structure.
successCriteria: The PermissionDemoComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, a selector, and an empty template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main component structure. This component will serve as the demonstration area for RBAC permissions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the component, but make sure to include the @Component decorator with selector and template properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't complete. Remember to create a class named PermissionDemoComponent with the @Component decorator.

steps.title: Initialize user role state in component
steps.instruction: In the PermissionDemoComponent class, add a property called currentUserRole and initialize it with a default role value like 'user'.
steps.hint: Add a public property in the component class with type annotation (e.g., currentUserRole: UserRole = 'user').
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a currentUserRole property initialized with a default role value.
successCriteria: The PermissionDemoComponent class contains a currentUserRole property with a default role value assignment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the user role state in the component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a currentUserRole property with a default value in the component class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have a properly initialized currentUserRole property. Try adding a property with a default role value.

steps.title: Inject PermissionService into component
steps.instruction: Inject the PermissionService into the PermissionDemoComponent constructor to make it available for use.
steps.hint: Add a constructor parameter with the PermissionService type and Angular will handle the dependency injection automatically.
steps.expectedOutcome: The PermissionDemoComponent constructor now has a parameter that injects the PermissionService.
successCriteria: PermissionService is injected as a constructor parameter
The service parameter has the correct type
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully injected the PermissionService into your component. This makes the permission checking functionality available throughout your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the PermissionService is properly typed as a constructor parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PermissionService needs to be injected as a constructor parameter with the correct type. Try adding 'private permissionService: PermissionService' to the constructor.

steps.title: Create template with permission-based elements
steps.instruction: In the PermissionDemoComponent template, add a button that uses the PermissionDirective to conditionally render based on the 'edit' permission.
steps.hint: Use the *appPermission structural directive with the required permission and role parameters.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: Button with permission check -->
<button *appPermission="'delete'; role: currentUserRole">Delete Item</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element that only appears when the current user role has 'edit' permission.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a permission-controlled button to the template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the button uses the *appPermission directive with both permission and role parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't include the required permission-based button. Review how to use the PermissionDirective.

steps.title: Add role switching functionality
steps.instruction: In the PermissionDemoComponent template, add a role selector with buttons to switch between 'admin', 'editor', and 'viewer' roles, and bind each button's click event to update the currentUserRole property.
steps.hint: Create three buttons with labels like 'Switch to Admin', 'Switch to Editor', and 'Switch to Viewer'. Use (click) event binding to call a method that sets currentUserRole to the corresponding role string.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: role switching in a component template
<button (click)="setRole('admin')">Admin</button>
<button (click)="setRole('editor')">Editor</button>
<button (click)="setRole('viewer')">Viewer</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include interactive buttons that allow the user to change roles and immediately see permission changes reflected in the UI.
successCriteria: Three buttons are present in the template with (click) event handlers that update currentUserRole to 'admin', 'editor', and 'viewer' respectively.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added role switching functionality. Now you can test how permissions change dynamically when switching between different user roles.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some role switching elements, but make sure all three roles ('admin', 'editor', 'viewer') have corresponding buttons with proper click handlers that update the currentUserRole property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The role switching functionality isn't complete. You need to add buttons for all three roles with click handlers that update the currentUserRole property to the corresponding role value.
